flags.note: The passive construction 'and was given to me' reflects Greek καὶ ἐδόθη μοι. Native Hebrew would more likely use active construction with God/angel as subject.
The passive 'it is given to the nations' mirrors Greek δέδοται τοῖς ἔθνεσιν. Hebrew would more naturally use active voice or construct with divine agency.
The use of שֶׁלִּי 'mine' as a possessive pronoun is typical of later Hebrew influenced by Aramaic/Greek patterns, rather than classical Hebrew construct chains.
While שֶׁ relative clauses are standard in Mishnaic Hebrew, the construction 'if someone' (εἰ τις) may reflect Greek influence on indefinite pronoun usage.
The negative purpose clause with שֶׁלֹּא mirrors Greek ἵνα μή construction, though this is acceptable in late Hebrew.
The temporal clause 'whenever they desire' with שֶׁ reflects Greek ὅταν θέλωσιν, though not unnatural in Hebrew.
The temporal clause 'when they complete' with שֶׁ corresponds to Greek ὅταν τελέσωσιν.
The relative clause 'that ascends' with שֶׁ mirrors Greek τὸ ἀναβαῖνον, though acceptable in Hebrew.
The causal clause 'because there' uses שֶׁ in a way that may reflect Greek ὅπου influence, though not impossible in Hebrew.
There appears to be a gap in the text before 'the prophets,' suggesting possible corruption or difficulty in translating the Greek ὅτι οὗτοι οἱ δύο προφῆται construction.
